```{r, include=F}
library(foreign)
library(tidyverse)
articles <- read.dta("http://www.stata-press.com/data/lf2/couart2.dta")

m_art <- glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, 
             family = poisson, data = articles)
#summary(m_art)
```

## Overdispersion

**Overdispersion** occurs when the response variable $Y_i$ has greater variability than the model accounts for.

\vspace{1cm}

**Poisson:** $Var(Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i) = \mathbb{E}[Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i] = \mu_i$

\vspace{2cm}

## quasi-Poisson models

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log(\mu_i) &= \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta} \\
Var(Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i) &= \phi \mu_i
\end{aligned}
$$

\vspace{6cm}


## Example: articles data

```{r, eval=F}
glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, family = poisson, data = articles)
```

```
             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
(Intercept)  0.276493   0.087294   3.167  0.00154 ** 
phd          0.008071   0.026358   0.306  0.75944    
ment         0.026537   0.002001  13.264  < 2e-16 ***
kid5        -0.099696   0.035248  -2.828  0.00468 ** 
(Dispersion parameter for poisson family 
   taken to be 1)
```

```{r, eval=F}
glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, family = quasipoisson, data = articles)
```

```
             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)  0.276493   0.119839   2.307   0.0213 *  
phd          0.008071   0.036184   0.223   0.8235    
ment         0.026537   0.002747   9.662   <2e-16 ***
kid5        -0.099696   0.048389  -2.060   0.0397 *  
(Dispersion parameter for quasipoisson family 
   taken to be 1.88461)
```

## Example: articles data

```{r, eval=F}
glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, family = quasipoisson, data = articles)
```

```
             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)  0.276493   0.119839   2.307   0.0213 *  
phd          0.008071   0.036184   0.223   0.8235    
ment         0.026537   0.002747   9.662   <2e-16 ***
kid5        -0.099696   0.048389  -2.060   0.0397 *  

(Dispersion parameter for quasipoisson family 
   taken to be 1.88461)

    Null deviance: 1817.4  on 914  degrees of freedom
Residual deviance: 1661.1  on 911  degrees of freedom
AIC: NA
```

## t-tests for quasi-Poisson models

$$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \approx N(\boldsymbol{\beta}, \phi (\mathbf{X}^T \mathbf{V} \mathbf{X})^{-1})$$

$H_0: \beta_j = b \hspace{1cm} Z = \dfrac{\widehat{\beta}_j - b}{\sqrt{\phi [(\mathbf{X}^T \mathbf{V} \mathbf{X})^{-1}]_{jj}}} \approx N(0, 1)$

\vspace{5cm}

## F-tests for quasi-Poisson models

The quasi-Poisson does not specify a full distribution.

\vspace{1cm}

But, the deviance still exists.

\vspace{5cm}

## Negative Binomial models

$$Y \sim NB(\mu, r) \hspace{1cm} f(y; \mu, r) = \frac{\Gamma(y + r)}{\Gamma(y + 1)\Gamma(r)} \left(\frac{\mu}{\mu + r} \right)^y \left(1 - \frac{\mu}{\mu + r} \right)^r$$

$$Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i \sim NB(\mu_i, r) \hspace{1cm} \log(\mu_i) = \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta}$$

\vspace{6cm}

## Example: articles data

```{r}
m3 <- MASS::glm.nb(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, data = articles)
```

```
             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
(Intercept)  0.233528   0.117585   1.986   0.0470 *  
phd          0.008203   0.036069   0.227   0.8201    
ment         0.030374   0.003240   9.373   <2e-16 ***
kid5        -0.093256   0.046475  -2.007   0.0448 *  

(Dispersion parameter for Negative Binomial(2.1647) 
   family taken to be 1)

AIC: 3145.6
```

## Inference for negative binomial models

* Can use the usual Wald tests for $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ (from asymptotic normality)
* LRT also works because a full distribution is specified

\vspace{7cm}

## Example: articles data

```{r}
m3 <- MASS::glm.nb(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, data = articles)
m4 <- MASS::glm.nb(art ~ phd + kid5, data = articles)

pchisq(m3$twologlik - m4$twologlik, 1, lower.tail=F)
```

\vspace{4cm}
